newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Six die, 25,000 flee as floods shut down Manila.
newsitem.headline: Six die, 25,000 flee as floods shut down Manila.

text.p: Six people died and 25,000 fled their homes on Tuesday as the fringes of Typhoon Winnie hammered Manila with torrential rains, officials said.

The downpour that began on Monday triggered widespread floods and power outages, forced the closure of government offices, businesses, schools and financial markets and caused traffic jams that were horrendous even by the notorious standards of the city of 10 million.
Philippine Airlines cancelled four international and 15 domestic flights and several other departures were delayed after crew members arrived late, the airport office said.
Several houses in the Manila suburb of Paranaque were flooded up to their rooftops, the town's mayor said.

"The floods were occasioned by the very heavy rains because of the tail of a very big typhoon," President Fidel Ramos told reporters, referring to Typhoon Winnie, which killed at least 31 people in Taiwan before slamming eastern China, where it killed five.

Four people drowned in Manila and nearby provinces, an old woman was crushed to death by a landslide in nearby Batangas and a man walking home in the floods in Malabon district was electrocuted by a fallen live wire, relief agencies said.
About 40 percent of the Philippine capital was flooded, officials said.
The weather bureau said it expected the rainy weather to last for two more days because of the prevailing monsoon.
"I was trapped on the expressway for nine hours last night," complained Ramon Lopez, a businessman.
Many commuters were ferried home in army trucks.
On the positive side, the rains brought a welcome respite to Manila's beleaguered stock and currency markets, which took a battering a day earlier.
